question.text: What is the LOWEST risk level shown on the Risk-o-meter?

explanation.text: The Logic: The lowest risk level on the Risk-o-meter is simply "Low" — not "Very Low" or "Zero Risk." This is important because even the safest mutual fund carries some risk. The Trap: There is no "Very Low" or "Zero Risk" category. The Risk-o-meter starts at "Low" because all mutual fund investments carry at least some level of risk. There is no guarantee of returns. Cross-Exam Context: Also tested in Series V-A. Remember: the 6 levels are Low, Low to Moderate, Moderate, Moderately High, High, Very High. Distributor's Pro-Tip: When clients ask for "zero risk" investments, explain that mutual funds always carry some risk. The lowest category is "Low" risk, typically seen in overnight funds or liquid funds.
